samples.summary: The canonical copy design doc still lists “REST v1 / CLI copy. Not exposed there; the web list is the only caller.” as a **Non-Goal**, and this change ships exactly that (`POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/copy` + `wafflebase docs copy`) without touching document-copy.md. The reversal is argued in agentic-office-workflow.md §3.1 and rest-api.md §5.1, so the decision itself is recorded — but the subsystem doc a reader consults for copy behavior now contradicts the shipped surface, and the repo's docs-by-subsystem discipline (CONTRIBUTING.md / docs/design/README.md) expects the reversal folded into the canonical doc rather than only asserted in the audit doc. Cost stays inside the codebase (a stale Non-Goal), hence minor rather than major.

The new folders controller in the same diff does reuse `CreateFolderDto`/`UpdateFolderDto`, so the change is internally inconsistent about layering, and — as the added test comment itself notes — the global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true })` validates nothing for an inline type, so the v1 rename accepts a title the web surface would reject and a non-UUID `folderId`. Reuse was available and directly applicable.

samples.summary: `ApiV1FoldersController.update`/`remove` reimplement the web `FolderController.update`/`remove` authorization and field-copy logic near verbatim (manager resolution via `assertMember` + `isDocumentManager`, the `name`/`parentId` split, `assertSameWorkspace`, `assertNoCycle`, identical Forbidden messages). Only `FolderService` is genuinely shared — rest-api.md §5.8 claims “one implementation”, which is true of the tree/cycle/delete but not of the authority rules. Two copies of the manager gate will diverge the next time one is fixed (the repo already shows this hazard: `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` exists because a per-handler check drifted). A small shared helper (or moving the gate into `FolderService`) was the fit here.

samples.summary: rest-api.md now contradicts itself about API-key authority. §3 still says “Neither it nor `WorkspaceScopeGuard` reads `scopes` — the guards prove the key is valid and bound to the workspace, nothing more”, and the §5 preamble (line 158-161) still says “For API key auth, the `:workspaceId` parameter must match the key's bound workspace. For JWT auth, workspace membership is checked via `WorkspaceService.assertMember()`” — i.e. membership is a JWT-only check. The diff makes `WorkspaceScopeGuard` assert the minter's live membership for API keys too, and only §5.8 records it. The two earlier passages are the ones a reader hits first.

samples.summary: Scope creep relative to the stated goal. The A′ close needs an `/api/v1` folder surface plus document copy/move; it does not need (a) a live-membership check for API keys in `WorkspaceScopeGuard` on every v1 route, (b) the same check hand-rolled in `ApiV1ImageReadController.assertCanRead`, (c) the manager gate newly applied to API keys on `DELETE /api/v1/.../documents/:did`, or (d) `WorkspaceService.removeMember` revoking keys inside a new transaction. These change the semantics of pre-existing endpoints and add a DB round trip per API-key request (including the hot image-read path). The docs were updated, and the tightening looks intentional and defensible, but bundling an auth-model change into a feature PR makes both harder to review and to revert independently.
